key_insight: A conservative finite-volume Darcy–Brinkman–Stokes formulation (DBS2) naturally retains second-Brinkman effects without separate discretisation, delivering near-DNS accuracy on voxelized rock images.
engineering_relevance: DBS2 enables accurate pore-scale flow and permeability prediction without boundary-conforming meshes while preserving DBS1’s computational efficiency.
method: Write the full DBS equation in conservative form.
Apply standard central differencing in a finite-volume discretisation to retain the complete viscous-stress contribution.
Implement DBS2 in GeoChemFoam and compare against DNS and simplified DBS1.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, DBS2 exactly reproduced the DNS microchannel velocity field and predicted micromodel and Bentheimer sandstone permeability within 1.5–3.8% of DNS at matched resolution, while DBS1 overpredicted permeability by 14.1–37.9%.
watch_item: Validation covers three benchmark cases; accuracy across broader rock geometries and voxel resolutions remains to be established.
paper_title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for Digital Rock Flow Simulation with Embedded Second-Brinkman Effects
